result.stdout:
PowerPortalsPro MCP server.

With no arguments it speaks the Model Context Protocol over stdio; MCP clients launch
it that way. The commands below are for setting up the Dataverse connection.

  login          Sign in to a Dataverse environment and bind it to this folder
  logout         Remove an environment from this folder
  status         Show which environments this folder uses, and whether each connects
                 (--environment <name> for one of them)
  environments   List the Power Platform CLI profiles available to mirror
  azure          Bind this folder to an Azure subscription (azure --help for more)

login options
  --environment <url>     The environment to bind, e.g. https://contoso.crm.dynamics.com.
                          An environment already bound can be named by its name or position,
                          to sign in to it again.
  --name <name>           What to call it — dev, test, anything. Renames one already bound.
  --make-primary          Make it the primary: the environment tools use unless told otherwise.
                          Works for a new environment and for one already bound (--primary for short).
  --pac-profile <name>    Take the environment and account from a Power Platform CLI profile
  --username <upn>        Sign in as a specific account
  --tenant <id>           Authenticate against a specific Entra tenant
  --browser               Open a browser instead of showing a device code
  --workspace <path>      Act on another folder

logout options
  --environment <name>    The environment to remove, by name, position or URL
  --all                   Remove every environment
  --forget                Also remove the saved sign-in for those environments
  --workspace <path>      Act on another folder

A folder can be bound to several environments — dev, test and production of one
customer, say. The first one bound is the primary; each later `login` with another
environment adds it after the others, unless you pass --make-primary. Agents act on
the primary unless as
[truncated]

result.stdout:
ppp-mcp azure — bind this folder to an Azure subscription.

  azure login           Sign in and choose the subscription this folder deploys to
  azure status          Show the bound subscription and whether it connects
  azure logout          Remove the subscription from this folder
  azure subscriptions   List the subscriptions the signed-in account can see

login options
  --role <role>         `hosting` or `registrations`, for a workspace whose app
                        registrations are owned in a different tenant from where the
                        portal runs. Only needed when it cannot be inferred
  --subscription <id>   Use this subscription instead of asking
  --tenant <id>         Authenticate against a specific Entra tenant. Needed when the
                        subscription belongs to a tenant you are a guest in
  --location <region>   Default region for resources, e.g. eastus
  --username <upn>      Sign in as a specific account
  --browser             Open a browser instead of showing a device code
  --workspace <path>    Act on another folder

logout options
  --forget              Also remove the saved sign-in for that tenant
  --workspace <path>    Act on another folder

This never reads or changes the Azure CLI's logged-in state. Each folder keeps its own
subscription, so several projects can target different customers at the same time. The
binding is written to .ppp/mcp.json and holds no secrets; the token is stored encrypted
in your user profile.
